you enjoy mastering difficult movement systems over time
not_for_you_if: you lack the patience for punishing platforming failures
you need working controller support and reliable physics
you expect endings and voice lines to function properly

claims.claim: Reviewers describe technical issues where the hammer passes through the floor, gets stuck at the bottom, or moves unpredictably due to buggy physics and unintended surface interactions.

citations.review_text: The sledge hammer just goes through the floor sometimes( lags to the other side of your body) and moving mechanics r buggy. The way it follows the mouse is plainly bad. Weird physics, rock it slippery, then not. When u try to move sometimes u jest get caught on random pixels, and going straight down with ur mouse will cause u to be stuck because the game thinks ur moving right/left when ur not.

This game is very unfair, I have completed it just 55 minutes after playing it for the first time but I have noticed some kind of wired things like the hammer goes to the bottom an get stuck there no matter how much you move your mouse, there was also a time where I just touched my mouse but the game registered a move by which I went down to all the way bottom.

I don't know how to feel about this game. I really like the philosophy and the message but i found the gameplay disappointing. It is very obvious the the mechanics are designed to make yo fail and get frustrated or angry and this makes sense based of the message. However I found the it isn't really hard its just done in a lame way. you could do it right but then it just does something random and shoots you across the map or something like that and I feel like this hurts the message. I fell multiple times and not once did I feel even a little bit frustrated I just felt bored. I think that the messaging of failing and learning and retrying and succeeding are lost because I one, couldn't get invested in the gameplay, two you don't learn from mistakes because if you do it might just mess up because the kettle is super bouncy now or the hammer just slides on something it never slid on before so fixing your mistakes doesn't help you progress. Finally I feel that there is no real sense of accomplishment or satisfaction when you finally succeed. I feel like part of the message is that by trying again after failing over and over you will at some point succeed and it will be worth it but I didn't feel anything when i succeeded. I was just bored because the gameplay took me out of it and the loop was not interesting to me. I think Elden ring did a better job of portraying this message because I would fight the same boss 30 times and every time I learned and adapted and when I finally defeated them I felt an accomplishment. This is because it was my skill or my choices that affected the out come and not just some random event. Overall I like the message and I really wanted to like the game. I have wanted to Play it for so long but I found myself disappointed and bored. I don't want to say its a bad game but i didn't enjoy it the way I thought I would.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game features voice narration and commentary that plays during gameplay.

citations.review_text:
Getting Over It with Bennett Foddy is not a game about climbing a mountain. It is a game about controlling your emotions while climbing a mountain.

The concept is simple: use a hammer to climb higher and higher through a ridiculous obstacle course. The controls feel awkward on purpose, and every small mistake can send you falling all the way back down. 🏔️🔨

What makes the game special is the psychological challenge. Every successful jump feels like a huge victory, while every fall tests your patience. Bennett Foddy's commentary somehow makes the experience even more frustrating and hilarious at the same time. 🎙️😂

The physics are unpredictable, the difficulty is intentionally brutal, and some sections can feel almost impossible at first. But when you finally master a difficult climb, the feeling of accomplishment is unmatched.

It is not a game for everyone. Many players will find the frustration overwhelming, and losing hours of progress can be painful. But if you enjoy challenging yourself, few games create the same emotional journey.

I came here to climb a mountain. I left questioning every decision that led me to buy a game where falling is the main feature. 😭

10% climbing. 90% psychological damage. 🪨💀

The most infuriating game I've ever played.  I've had it for years and never beaten it because I keep quitting. 
10/10 would recommend playing it, buy you will likely lose your sanity. The narration while you play is a nice touch and either makes it more bearable, or 10x more rage inducing, depending on the timing.

[h3] ⭐ Frustrating, Brilliant, and Somehow Impossible to Quit [/h3]

[code] [quote=Wendrex] 🇺🇸 Review (English)
⭐ Frustrating, Brilliant, and Somehow Impossible to Quit

🎮 First Impressions
Getting Over It with Bennett Foddy looks deceptively simple, but within minutes it becomes clear that it's about much more than climbing obstacles. It's a game about patience, persistence, and learning from failure. Your first session will probably include equal parts curiosity, frustration, and the irresistible urge to give it one more try.

🔥 Gameplay
The entire game revolves around controlling a hammer with nothing but your mouse. It feels awkward at first, but once you begin to understand the physics and how each movement affects your momentum, the controls become surprisingly satisfying.

What truly sets the game apart is its commitment to consequences. A single mistake can erase several minutes of progress, yet it rarely feels random. Every successful climb is earned through practice, precision, and improved execution rather than luck.

🎨 Graphics & Audio
The visuals are intentionally simple, allowing the obstacle design and physics to take center stage. Every object serves a purpose, making the environment easy to read while remaining surprisingly memorable.

Bennett Foddy's narration is one of the game's greatest strengths. His commentary often appears after setbacks, adding humor and thoughtful reflections that give the experience a unique personality. The minimal soundtrack also helps maintain the tension throughout the climb.

⚖️ Difficulty & Progression
This is an unforgiving game, but it's remarkably fair. There are no upgrades, checkpoints, or shortcuts to rely on. Progress comes entirely from improving your own skill and understanding of the mechanics.

One of the most rewarding moments is realizing that sections which once seemed impossible eventually become routine through practice alone.

claims.claim: The initial playthrough is described as very difficult and frustrating, but subsequent runs become significantly easier and faster once players learn the movement system.

citations.review_text:
This 'rage' game has a lot more depth than that label might suggest. Beating Getting Over It for the first time will most likely come with both satisfaction and a sense of relief that you're finally done. Therefore, if you often find yourself not willing to do repeat playthroughs, this game might not be worth your attention - it gets better the more time you invest in it.

While your first playthrough is most certainly going to be a slog, it's absurd how much better the movement system feels after only a few completions. What made me like this game enough to beat it over 150 times is this movement system - it was very unintuitive at the beginning but now, with some practice, it is extremely freeing. It's a speedrunner's dream. 

[b] You [/b] dictate the pace of the game and thus, the more confident your movement is, the more fluid it feels. You learn how to beat sections, which previously took you minutes, in mere seconds, and leap over large gaps with bold movement you weren't ready for before.

Setting a goal, achieving it, and trying to succeed at an even tougher goal is what Getting Over It boils down to for me, and if you think, this is an experience you are likely to share, try it out!
getting over the mountain the first time feels impossible, second time feels a bit easier, everything past that is braindead easy somehow
Ill be honest, you first run through is really rough. Once you complete it for the first time, it becomes less infuriating and more fun, especially when you find better ways to beat the game

The first run is famously very hard and rage inducing. Took me 3 hours and 33 minutes on my first time getting over it. Now I've gotten over it 54 times and my fastest run is 4 minutes and 54 seconds, and I have no intent of stopping here. Very enjoyable game once you learn how to play properly, highly recommend this game.

oddly relaxing after your second or so attempt. The skill floor on this game is what causes the majority of the rage you hear about, every attempt after my second took less than 20 minutes to reach the top.

edit: just hit 50 summits, might play more, not masochism it just gets fun once you get through the begininng

The learning curve is very steep with this game, especially in the beginning. Taking time and not panicking for sure helps. Would recommend, it is definetly worth the money, and a bit different from other games as well.

Completing the first run feels especially like an accomplishment, all the runs afterwards are much easier, setting a new PB time is then the new goal, feels nice though as well.

Took me about 6.5 hours for the first attempt, at 24 hours playtime I have now scaled the mountain 50x times and got the golden pot (~10 min per run at the end).
Pretty sure I'm done playing this game though, can still be quite frustrating at times 😅

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the voiceover narration features commentary from the creator, but point out that the dialogue does not change or add new lines during repeat ascents.

citations.review_text:
I believe it's a lot more fun to watch someone play this game on youtube than to play it yourself, so I don't think I can recommend you to play it. I do recommend supporting the creator and his other work tho!

The game isn't really difficult if you analyze it, it is designed in a very frustrating way however. The obtacles you encounter aren't hard to get through by themselves (maybe with 1 or 2 exceptions), but it is hard to get through them due to lack of checkpoints and how much you lose focus overtime. It's kind of a brilliant design actually.

I really wish there was more to the voiceover, some really intresting stuff gets brought up by the creator. If you play the game once you heard all of it unfortunately. There's no comment on you ascending the mountain again, no secret dialogue for speedrunning, nothing for getting all the achivements either. I think it'd really add to the experience if there was more. There's like... 6-8 minutes of it I think? Which is very little compared to the first playthrough you'll do.

The game is HORRIBLY optimized ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, I think the whole map and all the props are loaded in at the same time or something?

Reaching the end is very cathartic, it's geniuently something you can be proud of if you managed to do it. The reward for it is cool too. (Or rather WAS cool beacuse it doesn't work since a while ago and over the few months I took to get 50 climbs it wasn't ever turned back on so I don't think it'll work again unfortunately).

Good rage game I suppose, but don't play it. Watch your favourite youtuber instead, unless you'd like to support the creator or want to experience pain that ultimately leads to a lot of pride once you get over it.

Went from being afraid to move forward to appreciating the privilege of climb. The "foddian" style has been remade a hundred times but many miss the point of the climb without the guidance of Bennett's narration. It's a lesson well taught and personally significant. I couldn't ask for more.
